column3: The Hebrew uses collective singular Amalek and repeats David’s name.
The Hebrew coordinates falling to the ground and bowing with “and”; BSB makes homage the purpose of falling.
The Hebrew explicitly says David spoke “to him”; BSB leaves the recipient implicit.
The Hebrew calls the fleeing group “the people”; BSB specifies “the troops.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew repeats “the young man reporting to him” and twice says “behold”; BSB substitutes “he” and condenses the presentation.
The Hebrew coordinates turning, seeing, and calling with “and”; BSB puts the first two in a “when” clause.
The Hebrew explicitly says he asked “me” and “I said to him”; BSB leaves those recipients implicit.
The Hebrew says “all my soul is still in me” and links it with “for”; BSB uses “my life still lingers” and “but.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew leaves the shared act by the men implicit; BSB supplies “did the same.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew describes him as the son of a sojourning man, an Amalekite; BSB splits this into two statements.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says to approach and strike him; BSB renders the commands as “Go, execute him!” It leaves the striker unnamed, where BSB supplies “the young man.”
The Hebrew introduces David’s words with “and he said to him”; BSB supplies “the Amalekite” and makes the statement prior with “For David had said.”
The Hebrew repeats the lament root in verb and noun.
The Hebrew names the bow without an explicit word for “Song” and introduces the written notice with “behold.”

The Hebrew says “not anointed with oil” without a separate word meaning “longer.” It names fields of contributions without explicitly naming grain.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew explicitly says “their life” and “their death”; BSB leaves the possessives implicit.
The Hebrew describes bringing up gold adornment onto their clothing; BSB uses “decked your garments.”
